A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RLCR study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained material across substantial additions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL training and evaluation on question answering and mathematics, alongside test-time scaling, classifier, and confidence-consistency experiments in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original ablations, synthetic prediction experiments, additional model evaluations, and calibration-baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The core RLCR reward, training procedure, SFT warmup, and confidence-based scaling methods remain. Section 4.6 adds a recommended inference variant that omits uncertainty analysis, while Appendix J introduces an answer-formatting instruction for SFT+RLCR. These are limited inference adaptations using existing trained models.

E1.justification: The original QA and mathematics coverage is retained. Appendix E.2 adds a synthetic five-arm next-draw prediction task with short observation sequences and an optional invalid answer, extending coverage to a controlled stochastic prediction environment. This is a limited diagnostic extension.

E2.justification: v2 adds generation-likelihood selection and weighted-voting baselines to the scaling comparison, RLCR-Log to the scoring-rule comparisons, and full-sequence calibration RL, masked calibration RL, and Abstention-RL in Appendix I. These substantially expand evaluated alternatives; the original Table 1 comparator set remains despite naming refinements.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce OLMo-2-7B-Instruct and Qwen-3-8B configurations, synthetic training on 10,000 examples with zero to five observations, controlled analysis-prompt variants with token-cost measurement, and an SFT prompt intervention. Appendix I specifies distinct baseline initialization, loss masking, and abstention evaluation procedures. Existing benchmark splits and primary evaluation metrics remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct ablations separating calibrated rewards from uncertainty prompting, Brier-versus-log reward-hacking experiments, confidence-distribution analyses, and an investigation of SFT answer-formatting failures. These address mechanisms and failure conditions absent from v1. The earlier classifier-capacity study is retained in Appendix G rather than removed.

E5.justification: The detailed benchmark tables change from point estimates to reporting 95% bootstrap confidence-interval half-widths for accuracy, AUROC, and Brier score in Tables 8–15. ECE remains without intervals. v1 already contains classifier-plot error bars, but v2 substantially broadens explicit uncertainty reporting; this does not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 remains unchanged, but numerous new results cover ablations, baselines, model families, and confidence distributions. The synthetic task reports 34.4% accuracy for RLCR-Brier versus 0% for RLCR-Log. The changed SFT prompt yields 49.8% OOD accuracy versus 43.8%, although Table 7's caption inconsistently says 48%. Some retained appendix estimates also change, including base CommonsenseQA accuracy from 88.9% to 88.6%.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the logarithmic-loss sign, the spherical score's outcome dependence, and the minimization convention. The consistency formulation is generalized from equality for exhaustive answer sets to a confidence sum at most one, with equality when exhaustive. The central theorem and Appendix A proof are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract relaxes the blanket claim of calibration improvement 'with no loss in accuracy' to improvement 'while maintaining strong accuracy.' The central contributions concerning joint incentives, calibration generalization, and confidence-based test-time scaling remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix J qualifies v1's forgetting hypothesis by attributing much of the SFT accuracy loss to reversible answer-formatting bias. v2 also distinguishes reward-learning benefits from prompting benefits, qualifies log-score reward hacking as dependent on the setting, explains modest ensemble gains, and discusses misleadingly favorable calibration on high-accuracy datasets.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly documents learning rates, a 0.1 warmup ratio, one training epoch, and A100/H100 hardware. These are disclosures about retained experiments, not evidence of changed original settings. The abstract adds access information for code, models, and demonstrations, while new experiments document baseline masking, initialization, and prompt interventions.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on confidence-weighted self-consistency, abstention rewards, forgetting, GRPO, and OLMo. Appendix I also acknowledges and evaluates an accuracy-preserving masked calibration approach. These refine comparison with prior research while retaining the original four-part related-work organization and central novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v2 tightens experimental and related-work prose, moves the classifier study from Section 4.5 to Appendix G, relocates training discussion to Appendix K, and reorganizes detailed results into Appendices L and M. Front matter and disclosures are updated. Much of the core exposition, conclusion, proof, and prompts remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds reward and synthetic-task displays, reliability histograms, confidence-variability plots, and ablation, baseline, and model-comparison tables. The scaling plot gains two comparator curves and an expanded legend. Existing tables merge shared accuracy cells and accommodate confidence intervals, while training and classifier figures move to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence supporting RLCR. Direct reward-versus-analysis ablations and relevant RL-calibration baselines address important attribution and comparison gaps in v1, while additional model families test broader applicability. Bootstrap intervals, essential training details, and the SFT formatting investigation improve transparency and interpretation. The Table 7 caption discrepancy limits precision for that result but does not outweigh these substantial gains.
